claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi eutectic alloy has a fine lamellar microstructure consisting of coupled FCC and ordered B2 phases.
Catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility arise from stress concentration along continuous B2 interfaces in this AlCoCrFeNi alloy.
Room-temperature severe plastic deformation will fragment the continuous lamellar morphology.
Annealing at 800-900°C will cause fragmented B2 to coarsen into a reticulated morphology without restoring continuous lamellae.
The 800-900°C window is below the B2 ordering temperature and above the BCC-phase recrystallization temperature for this alloy.
Hydrostatic pressure above 5 GPa during severe plastic deformation will suppress void formation.
A deformation strain rate above 0.1 s^-1 is an appropriate condition for successful treatment.
Oxygen content above 0.8 wt% causes excessive hardening and brittleness.
The treatment will produce a discontinuous reticulated B2 network embedded in a continuous BCC matrix.
Fragmenting continuous B2 lamellae eliminates a continuous brittle crack-propagation path.
A reticulated intermetallic-phase morphology can improve ductility.
The reticulated B2 phase will impede dislocation motion and thereby provide strengthening.
A continuous BCC matrix surrounding the reticulated phase will accommodate plastic strain and improve ductility.
High pressure during severe plastic deformation will maintain density and prevent oxide-induced brittleness.
The treatment will raise uniform tensile ductility above 10% at room temperature.
The ductility increase will occur without a proportional loss in yield strength.
The treated material will avoid catastrophic interfacial cracking during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Conventional hot isostatic pressing preserves the original lamellar morphology because it does not provide the required fragmentation.
A continuous ordered-B2 matrix causes poor room-temperature ductility in B2+BCC refractory high-entropy alloys.
Excessive annealing-driven coarsening will reduce strength.

contradictions.description: The initial target alloy is described as FCC+B2, whereas the proposed product is B2 in a continuous BCC matrix. The intervention explains fragmentation and coarsening of B2 but does not specify or support the implied disappearance or transformation of the FCC phase into BCC.

Extreme pressure above 5 GPa is specified only for the SPD step, but the HIP control is described as using the same pressure as the annealing step, whose pressure is not defined. The proposed control therefore does not clearly isolate extreme pressure and also differs by the presence or absence of severe strain.
